title: Voice note to long-form presenter video
rationale: The whole production path in one task: a rambling voice note becomes a scripted talk, a presenter who stays the same person and in lip sync for minutes, B-roll that matches what is being said, and an edit with no visible seams. Short clips hide drift; four minutes does not. Contestants are routes rather than single models, so a compiled route and the raw avatar model it calls can meet head to head.
prompt: Turn the supplied voice note (fixtures/long-form/voice-note.json) into a finished talking-head video of at most eight minutes, presented by the person in the supplied character sheet. Clean the voice note into a script that keeps the speaker's points and order, add B-roll over the presenter where it illustrates what is said, and burn in captions. One continuous presenter; no music.
rubric: Does the script keep every point of the voice note, in order, and nothing it did not say?
Does the presenter stay the same person, with lips in sync, from first second to last?
Are the joins between presenter renders invisible?
Does each B-roll shot show what is being said at that moment?
Do the captions match the speech word for word?
Does it hold attention: pacing, cuts and length
